question: Why would a trader split a large order into smaller ones?
intro: A large order sent all at once walks the book and pays more for each price level it reaches. A trader who can wait sends it in slices, giving the market time to offer more at the better prices between them.

steps.ask: A buyer needs 20, but sends only 10, at 101. What would 20 at once have cost, and why might it wait?
steps.say: 20 at once would have taken 10 at 101 and 10 at 102: 2,030. Instead it buys only the 10 at the best price, 1,010, and waits.
The maker offers 10 at 101 again, refilling the best price.

steps.ask: The buyer sends its second slice, 10 at 101. What has it paid for all 20, against 20 at once?
steps.say: Another 10 at 101: 2,020 for all 20, 10 less than sending them at once. Slicing saved money because the maker refilled the best price. A maker that noticed the same buyer coming back might not: it could raise its offer instead. The slices make a pattern, of the same side and size, that others can learn to see.
